title: King’s Cup – rules

rules.h1sub: Drinking game rules & all card meanings

sub: Also known as Ring of Fire or Circle of Death: a deck of cards in a circle, a cup in the middle and a rule for every card. Read it once, draw, done.

seo.rulesT: King’s Cup Rules – Ring of Fire Drinking Game
seo.rulesD: King’s Cup (Ring of Fire, Circle of Death) explained: setup, what every card from Ace to King means, the four Kings, variants and how to play responsibly.

goal: The goal: Draw cards in turn, follow the rule of each card – and hope you’re not the one who draws the fourth King.

info.similar: Ride the Bus, Beer Pong, Never Have I Ever
info.gearAlt: A deck of cards and a big cup
info.intro: King’s Cup is the classic for hostel common rooms and pre-drinks: no strategy, no score sheet, just a deck of cards and a rule for every card. Everyone knows a slightly different version – so agree on the rules before the first card.

setupLead: Two minutes and you’re ready to go.
setup1: One standard deck of 52 cards, without Jokers.
setup2: A big empty cup in the middle of the table – the King’s Cup.
setup3: A drink for everyone – with or without alcohol, whatever each person likes.
setup4: 3 to 12 players, sitting in a circle around the table.
setupP: Shuffle the cards and spread them face down in a closed ring around the cup, so that every card touches its neighbours. The youngest player starts, then play goes clockwise.
turnLead: On your turn you draw one card from the ring and do what it says.
s1p: Take any card from the ring – carefully, without opening a gap.
s2p: Turn it face up so everyone can see it.
s3p: Every rank has its own rule (see The cards). Then it’s the next player’s turn.
breakP: If you open a gap in the ring while drawing, you take a sip as a penalty. In many groups, whoever breaks the ring has to drink the King’s Cup straight away – agree on this beforehand.
cardsH: The cards from Ace to King
cardsLead: The rank decides what happens, the suit doesn’t matter. These are the most common rules:
c_aP: Everyone starts drinking as soon as you start. Nobody may stop before the person to their right stops – you can stop whenever you like.
c_2P: Pick someone: they take a sip.
c_4P: Everyone touches the floor. The last one to do it takes a sip.
c_7P: Everyone points to the ceiling. The last one takes a sip.
c_8P: Choose a mate: whenever you drink, they drink too – until the next 8 is drawn.
c_9P: Say a word. Going round the circle, everyone says a word that rhymes. Whoever hesitates or repeats one takes a sip.
c_10P: Pick a category, e.g. beer brands or capital cities. Going round, everyone names something that fits. Whoever can’t think of anything takes a sip.
c_jP: Make up a rule that applies until the end of the game, e.g. “no first names” or “only drink with your left hand”. Whoever breaks it takes a sip.
c_qP: You are the Question Master until the next Queen. Whoever answers one of your questions takes a sip – unless they reply “Screw you, Question Master”.
c_kP: Pour a little of your drink into the cup in the middle. What happens with the fourth King: see The Kings.
cardsP: Many groups swap individual cards for their own rules – that’s part of the game. Good ideas are under Variants.
kingsLead: The Kings decide when the game ends.
kingsP: The fourth King: Whoever draws it has to drink the King’s Cup – in as many sips as they need. It doesn’t have to be in one go, and nobody has to finish a cup they don’t want to.
endP: The game ends with the fourth King. If you want to keep playing, shuffle all the cards, rebuild the ring and start again with an empty cup.
safeLead: King’s Cup should be fun for everyone – including the next morning.
safe1: Only for adults of legal drinking age in your country.
safe2: Always sips, never shots. Agree on small sips before you start.
safe3: No one has to drink alcohol. Water, soft drinks and alcohol-free beer count just as much – including in the King’s Cup.
safe4: Nothing gross in the cup. Only pour in drinks that go together, and never mix in anything that people don’t know about.
safe5: Have water on the table, take breaks, and never drive after playing. If someone has had enough, they’re out – no discussion.
varLead: King’s Cup is played differently at every table. Agree before the first card which of these rules you use:
var1: Gender-neutral 5 and 6: 5 becomes Thumb Master (put your thumb on the table at any moment, the last one to copy you takes a sip), 6 becomes Never have I ever.
var2: 4 = Social: Instead of touching the floor, everyone raises their glass and drinks together.
var3: 7 = Buzz (Seven): Count around the circle; on every number containing a 7 or divisible by 7 (7, 14, 17, 21 …), you clap instead. Whoever gets it wrong drinks.
var4: 8 = Snake Eyes: You become the Snake until the next 8: anyone who looks you in the eye takes a sip.
var5: J = Never have I ever: Everyone holds up three fingers; whoever has done what you name lowers one and takes a sip.
var6: Break the ring, drink the cup: Whoever opens a gap must drink the King’s Cup immediately, even before the fourth King.
var7: Without alcohol: Instead of sips, players collect points or do small dares; the fourth King has to sing a song or tell an embarrassing story.
faq1q: Is King’s Cup the same as Ring of Fire and Circle of Death?
faq1a: Yes. It’s the same game with different names – depending on the country and group, also simply “Kings”. Only the rules for individual cards vary.
faq2q: How many players do you need?
faq2a: At least three, it gets really fun with five or more. With more than twelve, it takes a long time before it’s your turn again – then use two rings.
faq3q: How long does a game last?
faq3a: Usually 30 to 60 minutes, depending on the number of players and how quickly the Kings come up.
faq4q: Do I have to drink the whole cup in one go?
faq4a: No. Take as many sips as you need – and if you don’t want to finish it, you don’t have to. See Play responsibly.
faq5q: How does the Waterfall work exactly?
faq5a: Whoever draws the Ace starts drinking and everyone else starts at the same time. Going clockwise, you may only stop once the person before you (to your right) has stopped. So the last one in the circle drinks the longest – go with small sips.
faq6q: What happens if the rule from the Jack contradicts another rule?
faq6a: The newer rule wins. If the table can’t agree, a vote decides.
faq7q: Can you play King’s Cup without alcohol?
faq7a: Absolutely. With soft drinks, water or alcohol-free beer the game works just the same – or you use small dares instead of sips (see Variants).
faq8q: Does the suit of the card matter?
faq8a: No, only the rank counts. Some groups make red and black cards different, e.g. red 2 = give a sip, black 2 = take a sip.
